T01: Make Redis dispatch recoverable and enforce shared worker concurrency

Own only: app/controllers/manager/base_manager.py, app/controllers/manager/redis_manager.py, test/services/test_redis_global_dispatch.py.

Evidence to reproduce:
The active-task counter is local to each manager (base_manager.py:47,55-68,98-129). Redis queue admission is atomic, but dequeue uses destructive LPOP (redis_manager.py:98-103) before execution is secured. Two managers can each consume the configured maximum, and a worker crash after dequeue can strand an accepted task.

Required change:
Implement a coherent Redis claim/lease protocol with atomic shared capacity reservation and release, plus recovery of claims that never reached execution. Keep local-manager behavior and queue-admission semantics compatible. Do not automatically repeat uncertain provider work after execution may have begun; expose a recoverable or failed state instead.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Two managers configured for a global limit of one never run two tasks simultaneously.
2. A crash between dequeue and execution cannot silently lose the task; demonstrate recovery or an explicit terminal state.
3. Completion, execution errors, and expired unstarted claims release capacity exactly once; startup recovery is safe.
4. Use isolated Redis fixtures or a faithful deterministic fixture; document any real Redis checks that could not run.

Focused validation:
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/services/test_redis_global_dispatch.py test/services/test_task_manager.py test/services/test_redis_queue_admission.py

tasks.title: Deduplicate concurrent paid TwelveLabs embedding requests
tasks.evidence: The embedding helper uses functools.lru_cache (twelvelabs.py:100-105). Concurrent misses for the same key may each invoke Marengo before the first result enters the cache, duplicating paid work.
tasks.deliverable: Add per-key synchronization so concurrent identical requests share one in-flight provider result. Preserve the cache key, bounded caching, existing client cleanup, and parallelism for different keys.
acceptance: Barrier/event-driven tests prove simultaneous same-key requests invoke the provider once.
Different keys can progress concurrently without a global serialization lock.
Provider failures wake all waiters, do not poison future attempts, and leave no stuck in-flight entries.
Existing cache and client-lifecycle tests pass; avoid timing-based sleeps and real provider calls.

VM environment setup (run before implementation; keep these setup steps out of your application diff):
Run the following self-contained Bash script inside your isolated Jules Ubuntu checkout. It installs locked development dependencies and local test fixtures without provider credentials. If the repository snapshot already has these dependencies, the commands remain safe to repeat. Keep the exported fixture variables set in the shell used for tests. Never connect the fixture tests to production Redis.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set +x
set -euo pipefail

# Run in the MoneyPrinterTurbo checkout inside a Jules Ubuntu VM.
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
python3 -m pip install --user --upgrade 'uv==0.12.5'
uv python install 3.11
uv sync --frozen --python 3.11 --extra twelvelabs

if ! command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null || ! command -v redis-server >/dev/null; then
    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ffmpeg redis-server
fi

# This daemon and database are dedicated to fixtures in the isolated VM.
export MPT_RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=0
export MPT_TEST_REDIS_HOST=127.0.0.1
export MPT_TEST_REDIS_PORT=6389
export MPT_TEST_REDIS_DB=15
if ! redis-cli -h "$MPT_TEST_REDIS_HOST" -p "$MPT_TEST_REDIS_PORT" ping >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    redis-server --bind "$MPT_TEST_REDIS_HOST" --port "$MPT_TEST_REDIS_PORT" \
        --save '' --appendonly no --daemonize yes \
        --pidfile /tmp/mpt-jules-redis.pid --dir /tmp
fi

uv run --no-sync python -m compileall -q \
    app cli.py main.py webui test docs/skill tools/sync_upstream.py
uv run --no-sync ruff check \
    app cli.py main.py webui test docs/skill tools/sync_upstream.py
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest -q \
    test/services/test_schema.py test/services/test_state.py

printf '%s\n' 'Jules environment ready: Python, locked dependencies, FFmpeg, Redis, lint, and smoke tests.'
```

tasks.title: Reject redirects on MiniMax voice-catalog POST requests
tasks.evidence: The MiniMax catalog requests.post call (voice.py:2246-2254) permits Requests' default redirect following. Other generation POST paths explicitly disable redirects. A 307/308 can replay the POST; 301/302/303 can trigger an unexpected follow-up GET.
tasks.deliverable: Disable redirect following for the catalog POST and explicitly reject all redirect statuses before parsing success data. Close rejected responses, keep errors bounded and redacted, and preserve normal 200 responses and existing catalog error handling. Do not describe this as proven cross-host authorization leakage.
acceptance: A mocked Requests transport covers 301, 302, 303, 307, and 308 and records exactly one POST with no follow-up request.
Redirect responses are closed and reported without exposing authorization headers or response payload secrets.
Normal catalog parsing, provider errors, and generation behavior remain compatible.
